body: shared.md:434, the documentation and test sprint archive step, keeps 'naming only paths that exist or that `git mv` removed'. It archives with git mv alone, so it shows no harm today; recorded only as the one other site of the old wording.

cmd_example probes <commit>:<path>, which git reads relative to the repository root, not the project root; where the project root sits below the repository root, approving a worked example by its project-relative path is refused. Out of this stage's brief.

tests::test_paths runs subprocess.run(['node', ...]); with node not on PATH it raises FileNotFoundError, which main's catch-all prints as 'tests: internal error: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: node' rather than a refusal naming the lint's requirement. Pre-existing, outside this stage's brief.

The checker prompt's intro lists the files whose every claim a brief may name as 'a file the run changed, ... changed since the stamp, ... not covered at its stamp, or any file of a docspec with no stamp'. Boilerplate step 7 now names every claim of each write or change item's file, changed or not, so the prompt's list omits a write or change item the run left unchanged; a checker reading the prompt over the brief may record such a file with scope stale, and docs complete then names it as unchecked.

The family CLAUDE.md layout line for skills/_sprint/shared.md lists 'the run rules and archive step of a documentation sprint and a test sprint' and does not name the new {{CEREMONY-VETO}} block (the veto step at their close); the description of the shared file is now incomplete.

body: Work item 'A test sprint writes support files first and runs its test tasks side by side' (and decision:test-support-written-before-tests: 'Each test task waits on the support tasks for the files it names, reads those files'): a test task is never told about the legacy support files its scenario uses. Path: tests tasks --stage write -> scripts/tests::stage_write -> support_of(plan, s) (s.support plus every plan legacy entry with sort=support whose scenarios name s) feeds only the --after waits; the test task's --files are its test path and old path, and its brief is scenario_brief(s), which prints 'Support: <s.support>' alone (scripts/tests:scenario_brief, 'if s.get("support"): parts.append("Support: %s." ...)'). {{TEST-WRITE-PROMPT}} tells the agent 'Your brief names ... its support files' and Read step 5 'Each support file your brief names, whole', and to record a helpers item where a helper is missing. So for a fixture a sort agent kept as legacy support (sorted_support derives entry.scenarios), the test task waits on its support task yet neither its brief nor its files name the fixture: it does not read it, and may record a missing helper for a helper that file holds, or write a test that ignores the fixture. At the base the test task held every legacy support file in --files, so it saw them; the change caused the loss when it moved support out of the test task's files. Scope: caused.

body: Trigger: a story in group:<n> is re-planned alone in a story:<slug> task before review (an assembly failure at step 8 or a runner re-plan at step 9 sends a judgment fix through 'Fixing a planner's items'). Path: SKILL.md step 11 files a review per latest done planner task, so group:<n> is reviewed with brief 'stories: <the stories its brief names>' (the group brief, which still names the re-planned story) -> core.md TEST-PLANNER-REVIEW-PROMPT Read step 1 reads every item whose task is group:<n>, in stories/scenarios/questions/legacy/calls, and Read step 2 reads each story the brief names. scripts/tests::planning_items (owners: the highest done story task holding a stories item) no longer takes that story's items from group:<n>, so the reviewer checks superseded items the plan does not hold and records findings with refile=group:<n>. The session then applies each finding as SKILL step 6 says: a judgment fix re-plans the story alone with 'revise task <the task its items came from>', and the revising agent (TEST-REVISION-RULE) refiles the items of the task its brief names; where that is the finding's refile task, group:<n>, the stale items are refiled under the new story:<slug> task, which then owns the story and replaces the correct re-plan. Harm: the owner's /plan-tests run reviews, and can act on, items the assembly discarded, giving a wrong plan or a needless re-plan (A3: a developer action through a script-driven skill gives a wrong result). Nothing in the review prompt or step 11 limits a planner review to the items the assembly takes from that task. Scope: caused by this change (the per-group review and the one-story re-plan are both new in this sprint).

body: Boundary: Trued-up projects (.ok-planner/release-boundaries.md). Its 'Not across it' leaves out only 'a sprint, documentation sprint, or test sprint in execution, and a planning run in progress'; a test sprint /plan-tests approved under v28 whose /goal has not started is across it. The notes rule B114 (and B105, B106, B107, B112) 'Across Trued-up projects: none; the boundary leaves out a test sprint planned earlier, whose -plan.json holds no folders, and one not yet executed is brought current before it runs.' Nothing brings a test sprint current: true-up's live-sprint rewrite reads only .ok-planner/sprints/ (admin/true-up::live_sprints, BOILERPLATE_SECTIONS from plan-sprint/sprint-document.md), and no skill step re-copies a test sprint's boilerplate or re-assembles its plan. Before: a v28 -plan.json with no 'folders' key ran , , the sweep, and  (all read tree_files(root) at the root). After: scripts/tests::plan_folders raises InputError 'the plan records no folders: assemble it again with ' from cmd_run --sprint (line 1420), stray_paths (1477), complete_failures (2060, 2084), and plan_failures (1147). The advised fix cannot run:  now needs the run's scope item (planning_scope: 'the planning run records no scope') and a -groups.json (read_groups), which a v28 planning run never wrote, and  itself refuses a run with no scope item. So the owner who runs /ok between approving a test sprint and starting it gets a test sprint that can never print TESTS COMPLETE, and the test-sprint-document boilerplate's own steps 5-7 stop on these refusals; the refusal names a step that also refuses. A plan with no 'folders' is an old plan the code could read as the root alone (no declared folders at planning), which is what it meant. Scope: caused by the change (plan_folders and its callers are new in this sprint; at the base these readers took the root).

The owned-set check no longer binds the resolve and amend owner-file writes to their consent paths. At the base, check_planner listed write_text and write_json as checked ops and allowed write_text(target_path)/write_json(target_path) only inside the resolve region and write_owner(target) only inside the amend region (git show 63de162:./checks/owned-paths lines 572-577: "target_path": ("resolve",), "write_json": {"target_path": ("resolve",)}, and the amend region). The change routes both writes through the new wrapper true-up::answer_write (resolve_question's review-config, reword, review-facts, stack-lines, config, and citation-tags branches; the amend mode's answer_write("amend:%s" ...)), drops the amend region and the target_path keys, and allows write_text(path) only inside answer_write (checks/owned-paths: "path": ("answer_write",)). answer_write is not itself among the ops check_sites checks (its sibling wrappers write_text, write_settings, write_file, and write_owner are), so a call answer_write(<id>, <any path>, <text>) from any mode or region of the core now passes the check. User: checks/run (project.md Scripts for developers), whose goal, read from the core's own constraint in ADMINISTRATION.md 'What the administration does NOT do here' (every other write goes 'through resolve ... or through amend'), is to fail when the core writes an owner file outside those consent paths; that goal now fails on the path of any future answer_write call outside resolve_question and the amend mode. A8: the plumbline cheatsheet's mechanical-checks rule (every written constraint needs a check that fails on violation), with the check's own sibling shape deciding the fix. Not listed among the notes' B-ids or the owned-paths Changes (which name the new regions and keys only). Scope: caused by the change (the back-out work item's owned-paths edit).

brief: story keep-documentation-current; drive name keep-documentation-current-2c114f9b

body: In a scratch project trued up from the working tree (stack run run-ef8c25237266), I wrote an approved sprint (one Amend story delta, one work item, the fixed completion contract copied from sprint-document.md), then asked .ok-planner/bin/review certified --sprint at each step. The verdict was right for: delta not landed, check failing, no completion report, report with no '# Sprint certification' block, defect open, stuck defect not listed, drive never ran, unapproved sprint, archived with closed: stamp, and SPRINT COMPLETE once every term held. Two outcomes were wrong. (1) Before the base file is written, certified gives no verdict and points at a flag it refuses: 'review: .ok-planner/sprints/cc2c-greeting.md records no base commit (no .ok-planner/sprints/cc2c-greeting-base.txt); pass --base' exit 1; then 'review certified --sprint ... --base 2340d85...' -> 'review: error: unrecognized arguments: --base 2340d85...' exit 2. (2) A second approved sprint, cc2c-farewell.md, whose work item (farewell.sh) was never built and on which no certification ever ran, printed 'SPRINT COMPLETE: .ok-planner/sprints/cc2c-farewell.md' exit 0. Its completion report named the first sprint's ledger (.ok-planner/review/runs/converge-2026-10-24T090000.jsonl): 'item 3 (certification): holds: the return block names .ok-planner/review/runs/converge-2026-10-24T090000.jsonl, the find loop ran, every defect is settled, 1 stuck defects are listed, and the drive ran over 1 stories'. certified checks that the named ledger holds a review task closed done and settled defects, but never checks that the ledger certified this sprint. The story promises: a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered, so that done means the same thing for every sprint; the contract's item 3 asks for the return block of sprint certification run on this sprint. saw: SPRINT COMPLETE for a sprint whose approved work was never delivered or certified, and no verdict at all (a message naming a refused flag) for an approved sprint whose base file is not yet written.

Reviewed /converge drive mode end to end (SKILL.md, prompts drive, merge, fix, verify, backout, owner-list, drain.md, scripts/review) and ran its verbs in a scratch project (stack run, true-up, two stories, tasks init, review prompt for every drive-mode prompt, review drives, merges --source drive, snapshot, fixes, verifies, drives --confirm --dry-run, drives --confirm, a confirm send-back, a second round to stuck, backouts): the mechanics deliver find, fix, verify, confirm, and backout. The divergence: in drive, analysis, and defects mode, review prompt fills [SPRINT PATH] and [BASE] with the word none (scripts/review assembled_lines, default sprint none), and merge.md is the one prompt that never says none means no sprint (fix.md says 'or no sprint where that reads none'; verify.md says 'where that reads none, no ruling does'). The assembled drive-mode merge prompt then reads, at merge.md:52: 'Where none names a sprint, this run certifies it from the base commit none, and the drive stays inside its scope: apply the sprint catalog's scope test to the function you named, reading it at the base. Where the code stood the same at the base and the sprint's change does not reach it, the defect is real but outside the sprint: tasks item set <failure id> --state backlog ... and merge nothing.' In plain English, 'where none names a sprint' holds exactly when no sprint is named, so a merge agent that reads it literally sends every real drive failure in a drive-mode run to backlog, unmerged: no fixer, verifier, or confirm driver sees it, and the break leaves the run unfixed as an intake issue. The same inverted condition stands at merge.md:31 ('where none names a sprint and its change deleted a file, add --base none'), merge.md:34 (the C3 bullet), merge.md:46 (the C4 entry), and merge.md:84 (the close counts). The story promises: 'to have each break that check finds fixed, so that a change that breaks a promise does not reach my users unnoticed'; decision converge-finds-then-fixes: 'The fix loop has fixers work through that list once.' Evidence: assembled file .ok-planner/review/runs/converge-test/merge.md in the scratch project, line 108: 'Where none names a sprint, this run certifies it from the base commit none, and the drive stays inside its scope'.

I reviewed /converge sprint (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md, prompts sprint-review.md, sprint-pass.md, merge.md, owner-list.md, drive.md, skills/_sprint/shared.md, skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md steps 12-13 and the completion contract) and the review script's certified verb it ends on. The return block's text does not say to name a stuck defect by its tracker id, but certified requires that id. SKILL.md The return: '- `fixed`: defects `verified`, `declined`, `duplicate`, and `stuck`, by entry of the accept list or sprint class' and '- `intake`: every issue the owner list wrote, turned, or closed, by id, with its category; each stuck defect with its last verifier's note and whether its backout closed `done`'. Neither line names the defect's item id; the only ids it asks for are issue ids. scripts/review certification_failures: 'elif defect["state"] == "stuck" and not re.search(r"\\b%s\\b" % re.escape(defect["id"]), "\\n".join(section)): failures.append("stuck defect %s is not listed in the return block in %s" ...)'. In a scratch project, a return block that listed the stuck defect without its item id gave: 'SPRINT NOT COMPLETE ... - stuck defect i2 is not listed in the return block in .ok-planner/sprints/cc2c-greeting-completion.md'; adding 'stuck: i2' gave SPRINT COMPLETE. sprint-document.md step 13 treats SPRINT NOT COMPLETE as a genuine blocker and stops. The story promises: done means the same thing for every sprint; decision sprint-goal-read-from-the-repository: 'A stuck defect the return lists ... is the owner's to take up, and holds no term of the contract open.' saw: a session that follows the return's text, listing each stuck defect by count per entry, by its note, or by the issue id the owner list filed, leaves the contract open on a sprint whose terms all hold, so whether done is reached depends on how the session happened to word the block.

body: Entry A8 (a commitment of a live design artifact, with one compliant form). Rule: decision:payload-citations-stripped-at-true-up, Choice: 'A markdown payload, such as a skill, carries no citation that resolves in the suite's own corpus, because its text may show a consumer the annotation's form.' Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/ok-version/SKILL.md:12 now reads '<!-- @story: see-governing-versions -->', added by build stage t6 (git diff 63de162 adds it above '### 1. Installed plugin version'). The family's skills are markdown payload that true-up vendors into consumer .claude/skills/, and .ok-planner/design/stories/see-governing-versions.md exists, so the citation resolves in this repo's corpus and in no consumer's. Mechanical evidence: checks/materialized-standalone walks MARKDOWN_PAYLOAD_TREES (ok-planner/skills among them) and appends 'skills/ok-version/SKILL.md:12 does not stand alone in a consumer: @story: see-governing-versions resolves in this repo's corpus and in no consumer's' for exactly this line, so the check, and checks/run (a developer script .ok-planner/review/project.md lists), exit 1 on a file the change touched. It is the only family markdown payload in the tree that carries a resolvable citation. Sibling stages met the same rule and kept it: t22 left the notes' <!-- @decision: pinned-build-placed-at-true-up --> out of skills/dashboard/SKILL.md (divergence i98) and t28 left <!-- @decision: drain-runs-as-a-workflow-script --> out of skills/_tasks/drain.md (i112), each naming checks/materialized-standalone. t6 recorded no divergence. Note for routing: the work item '/ok-version's story promises the installed plugin version' and the notes' call at sprint line 1107 asked for this line; that call cites plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md:50 as its sibling, but the front door's own skill lies outside the trees the check reads, so the sibling does not carry over. The decision and the check leave one compliant form for a family skill: no resolvable citation. Scope: caused by the change (the line is new; the base file held no citation).

body: Reviewed /converge (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md, every prompt under prompts/, _converge/coding-rules.md, scripts/review, scripts/issues, triage-issues/SKILL.md). Also ran the mechanical find-to-fix path in a scratch project trued up from the working tree: issues file (defect issue naming app/store.py:save) -> review backlog (1 report; a suite-file issue settled with left_alone {accept.md: suite}) -> defect item -> review snapshot -> review fixes --round 1 (t1) -> tasks close refused done while the defect stood fixing (exit 2) -> fixed -> review verifies (t2) -> verified -> issues close --as fixed -> tasks calls 'None.'. That path works. The divergence is in how the owner list avoids handing the owner a question the owner already judged. The owner list checks only OPEN issues before it files: owner-list.md:32 'First read `issues list --json` for an open issue on the same harm; where one stands, write nothing', :42 '... for an open issue on the same question ...', :61 '... for an open issue on the same defect ...' (and the defect route: 'First read `issues list --category defect --json` for an open issue at the same site'). Nothing in the owner list, the merge, or triage reads the archive (.ok-planner/history/issues.jsonl, `issues history`) for a closed issue on the same question. So a question the owner already settled without a corpus change comes back on the next run that meets it: (1) a story that is always blocked locally (needs real hardware or a hosted provider) produces an `environment` failure every drive, and the owner list files 'every other drive failure at `environment`' as a tooling judgment issue whenever none is open; once the owner retires it in /plan-sprint, the next drive files it again; triage routes it `question` again, because a retirement is not 'a live corpus artifact' that settles it; (2) an upstream issue the owner filed upstream, which /plan-sprint closes `answered`, is filed again by the next run whose agent meets the same suite-file harm or records the same proposal, and triage keeps it open 'while the project shows the harm', so /plan-sprint walks it with the owner again; (3) a merge's two-readings `question` on a story the owner retired without changing it is asked again on the next drive. The story promises: 'so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment'; decision intake-writers-are-gated: 'An agent that filed every observation as a question would be an ungated writer inside a repeating cycle, growing the queue run after run' and 'Deduplication against the slugs already present is the standing discipline of every writer into the intake'. Saw: the owner list's dedupe covers open issues alone, so a judged-and-closed question returns to the owner's agenda run after run.

body: Reviewed /plan-docs (SKILL.md, core.md, doc-sprint-document.md) and drove plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs on a scratch project. The skill text treats only a docspec with NO stamp as needing every claim checked, but docs window also reports status new for a docspec whose stamp the repository no longer holds (after a rebase), with that stamp still set. Diverging lines: SKILL.md step 2 defines "new (no stamp: its documentation is written whole)"; core.md DOC-PLANNER-PROMPT step 3 "For a docspec with no stamp, every file the layout calls for ... the run checks every claim in it"; DOC-CHECK-PROMPT "or in any file of a docspec with no stamp"; DOC-STYLE-PROMPT runs "git diff <stamp> -- <file>" and says only "For a docspec with no stamp ... the whole file changed"; doc-sprint-document.md step 7 keys full checks to "the docspec has no stamp" while its Window line records "its stamp or none", so the executor sees a stamp. The story and decisions promise: docspec-stamp-opens-the-window "A docspec with no stamp, or with a stamp the repository no longer holds, is planned as new: its missing files are written whole, and every claim in its existing files is checked"; documentation-claim-ledger "checks every claim ... in every file of a docspec planned as new". Saw: with doc-state stamp set to 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567, docs window --json printed "stamp": "0123...", "status": "new", "stale_claims": 0, reason "stamp ... is not a commit this repository holds, as after a rebase; the docspec is planned as new", while docs claims greet-reference --stale listed all 4 ledger claims (count disagrees); git diff 0123... -- docs/greet-flags.md printed "fatal: bad object 0123..." exit 128. A check item in such a docspec then gets only the ledger ids rechecked, docs complete passes with one claim per check file, and claims in the text that are not in the ledger are never checked, so the update can ship documentation that does not describe the product as it stands.

Followed the documentation sprint boilerplate (doc-sprint-document.md) on a scratch project through a drop item: the writer prompt (core.md DOC-WRITE-PROMPT) says "Any other drop runs git rm <file>"; then the archive step the boilerplate names, CEREMONY-ARCHIVE in skills/_sprint/shared.md, step 2: "Commit those paths alone with git commit -- <paths>, naming only paths that exist or that git mv removed". A path git rm removed neither exists nor was removed by git mv, so a session that follows the text leaves the dropped document out of the commit. The story promises that after each update a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands; decision docspec-stamp-opens-the-window has planning "plan a drop of each one no standing docspec covers". Saw: tasks close t1 --staged docs/greet-flags.md and docs complete printed DOCS COMPLETE; the commit naming only existing paths (5 archive files) left git status "D  docs/greet-flags.md" and git ls-tree HEAD docs/ still listed docs/greet-flags.md; git commit --dry-run -- docs/greet-flags.md exits 0, so naming the removed path works. docs stamp then stamped the docspec at that commit and docs window printed "status: current", and for a retired docspec the stamp removes its run state, so no later window finds the dropped file: the committed documentation keeps a file the run dropped.

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md in phase order (2 Frame, 3 Reconcile, 4 Dialogue, 5 Draft, 6 Resolve). The skill settles and drafts work at Frame, before Reconcile has walked the out-of-band changes. Reconcile's own rule says that must not happen. Frame, ruled sweep (SKILL.md section 2): 'For each ruled issue, carry the ruling's substance into the draft in final form — corpus delta, work item, or both — exactly as if the owner had just decided it live.' Frame, intake-drain kind: 'Run the issue walk (under Resolve) over that scope now, then the dialogue ... and the draft'. The walk's Promote step then says: 'Record the decision verbatim as the issue's ruling ... Then carry the substance into the sprint now, in final form'. Reconcile (section 3) says: 'The corpus catches up with such work here, before anything is drafted on top of it.' No step tells the session to re-base a final-form amendment from Frame, or a ruling recorded in the walk, onto a Reconcile outcome on the same artifact. An amendment carries the whole body ({{CORPUS-DELTA-FORM}}: 'Author an amendment by editing the artifact during planning and carrying the whole result'). So a ruled-issue amendment drafted before Reconcile can silently drop a 'Corpus catches up' change to the same artifact, or stand as a second amend delta on it. In an intake-drain session, the owner also rules each open question against a corpus that surface-corpus reads before out-of-band work is reconciled. The story promises: my goals, and the open questions and unreconciled work that bear on them, become one self-sufficient sprint that any executor can realize without re-deriving my intent. Saw: the phase order lets ruled and walked resolutions be drafted on top of unreconciled work. The skill gives no step that merges the two, so the executor or certification would have to re-derive which body is meant. Evidence: SKILL.md section 2 lines quoted above (Frame, 'Pull in the ruled issues first' and the 'Intake-drain sprint' bullet), section 3 first paragraph, and the section 6 'Promote' paragraph.

body: Reviewed the port path end to end: the sort prompt (core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT) says only 'A port's check is a program outside every test path, such as checks/<rule>, that takes the changed files' paths as arguments'. The legacy prompt (TEST-LEGACY-PROMPT step 2) says 'write the check at the path the brief names, outside every test path' and records 'command="<the command review checks runs, such as python3 checks/<rule>>"'. Then scripts/tests cmd_ports appends every recorded command to .ok-planner/review/config.json checks with no test-runner check (lines 1822-1837), and complete_failures only checks that each command is present (lines 2041-2043). Nothing in either prompt or either verb keeps the command from starting with a test runner, as a straight port of a pytest or jest fitness test naturally does. scripts/review cmd_checks then refuses the whole checks list. Drove it in a scratch project (stack run run-19b5f912af32, since taken down): with a checks entry 'python3 -m pytest -q checks/test_arch.py', '.ok-planner/bin/review checks --base HEAD --key gate2' printed: review: .ok-planner/review/config.json 'checks' runs tests through 'python -m pytest' in 'python3 -m pytest -q checks/test_arch.py'; tests run only inside a test sprint, or when a person asks for a run, so take it out of 'checks' and exited 1. So a port written this way passes 'tests complete' and then stops every project check from running at review, the ported rule included. The story promises: the old suite does not leave a rule it enforced unchecked. Decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically says: 'A rule a fitness check enforced still needs a check after the test goes, and the review loop's checks run on every review.' Saw: a ported check that review checks refuses leaves that rule unchecked, and every other check too. Where the harness offers the Workflow tool, the session starts the drain script once and the script returns only on done, waiting, stuck, paused (950 agents), or failed; a sprint whose stages chain with --after drains in one script call, because next issues each dependent stage as its predecessor closes. sprint-document.md step 6 says: 'Mark an entry in progress when the drain that runs its build task starts', so every stage, blocked ones included, goes in progress at drain start; drain.md 'When it returns' step 3 says: 'mark the entry for each task in closed whose outcome is done as done', so every stage goes done at once when the whole drain returns. The checklist shows nothing landing during the run. The story promises: 'the stages of a running sprint shown as a live checklist in my session, each marked as it lands, so that I can follow a long run without opening the completion report.' Saw: in the Workflow form, the default where the harness offers it, no entry is marked as its stage lands; the owner sees all stages in progress until the run ends, then all done. Note: decision task-tools-mirror-the-report accepts this ('Where a Workflow script runs the drain, the session marks each entry from the closed tasks the script returns, each time it returns'), and decision drain-runs-as-a-workflow-script makes the session wake once per drain, so the story and the two decisions disagree; the fix may be a script that returns per closed stage or an amended story, an owner question.

Reviewed /plan-docs (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-docs/SKILL.md, core.md, doc-sprint-document.md) for the no-internal variant. Saw: {{DOC-EDIT-RULES}} in core.md:17 reads '| An element the surface intent keeps internal appears. | Remove it. |' with no condition on ## Lists, and it is transcluded into the planner and every writer prompt; the writer prompt at core.md:228 reads 'A doc comment on an internal element goes.', for every in-code docspec. Reviewed /converge (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md, every prompt under prompts/, _converge/coding-rules.md, scripts/review, scripts/issues, triage-issues/SKILL.md). Also ran the mechanical find-to-fix path in a scratch project trued up from the working tree: issues file (defect issue naming app/store.py:save) -> review backlog (1 report; a suite-file issue settled with left_alone {accept.md: suite}) -> defect item -> review snapshot -> review fixes --round 1 (t1) -> tasks close refused done while the defect stood fixing (exit 2) -> fixed -> review verifies (t2) -> verified -> issues close --as fixed -> tasks calls 'None.'. That path works. The divergence is in how the owner list avoids handing the owner a question the owner already judged. The owner list checks only OPEN issues before it files: owner-list.md:32 'First read `issues list --json` for an open issue on the same harm; where one stands, write nothing', :42 '... for an open issue on the same question ...', :61 '... for an open issue on the same defect ...' (and the defect route: 'First read `issues list --category defect --json` for an open issue at the same site'). Nothing in the owner list, the merge, or triage reads the archive (.ok-planner/history/issues.jsonl, `issues history`) for a closed issue on the same question. So a question the owner already settled without a corpus change comes back on the next run that meets it: (1) a story that is always blocked locally (needs real hardware or a hosted provider) produces an `environment` failure every drive, and the owner list files 'every other drive failure at `environment`' as a tooling judgment issue whenever none is open; once the owner retires it in /plan-sprint, the next drive files it again; triage routes it `question` again, because a retirement is not 'a live corpus artifact' that settles it; (2) an upstream issue the owner filed upstream, which /plan-sprint closes `answered`, is filed again by the next run whose agent meets the same suite-file harm or records the same proposal, and triage keeps it open 'while the project shows the harm', so /plan-sprint walks it with the owner again; (3) a merge's two-readings `question` on a story the owner retired without changing it is asked again on the next drive. The story promises: 'so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment'; decision intake-writers-are-gated: 'An agent that filed every observation as a question would be an ungated writer inside a repeating cycle, growing the queue run after run' and 'Deduplication against the slugs already present is the standing discipline of every writer into the intake'. Saw: the owner list's dedupe covers open issues alone, so a judged-and-closed question returns to the owner's agenda run after run.
note: two readings: the owner list's dedupe covers open issues alone, so a judgment the owner closed (retired, or an upstream issue answered) may be filed again; the first reading: 'the slugs already present' are the open intake's, so refiling a closed question is owed behavior and the owner meets it again only when a run meets it again; the second: a question the owner already judged no longer 'needs my judgment', so writers also dedupe against the archive; the first rests on decision intake-writers-are-gated, Choice: 'Deduplication against the slugs already present is the standing discipline of every writer into the intake'; the second on story find-and-fix-defects: 'so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment'

body: What the product does: /converge's owner list (skills/converge/prompts/owner-list.md, lines 32, 42, 61) checks only open issues before it files, and neither the merge nor triage reads the archive, so a judgment the owner closed without a corpus change (an environment failure retired, an upstream issue answered after filing upstream, a two-readings question retired) is filed again by the next run that meets it. The two readings: (1) dedupe against open issues alone is what is owed, by decision intake-writers-are-gated: 'Deduplication against the slugs already present is the standing discipline of every writer into the intake'; (2) a closed judgment is a question that no longer needs the owner, so writers dedupe against the archive too, by story find-and-fix-defects: 'so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment'. Reviewed the sort table in core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT. Only one row ports a test: 'It enforces a written rule on the code's shape, such as a module boundary or a naming rule. | port'. Its read list limits the rules a sort agent looks for to 'the decisions under .ok-planner/design/decisions/, the practices under .ok-planner/practices/, .ok-planner/release-boundaries.md, and the rules files under .claude/rules/'. Every other test falls to 'It checks the code against itself, or a behavior no story or rule names. | delete, as an orphan'. A project that is just adopting the suite has a thin corpus, so a fitness test that enforces a layering or naming rule no decision, practice, or rules file states yet is sorted 'delete, orphan'. The sort raises no question for it (by design, decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically), records no call, and files no issue asking the owner to write the rule down. tests plan --show then lists it only as 'delete, orphan' among the other orphans. The story promises: the old suite does not leave 'a rule it enforced unchecked'. That covers any rule the old suite enforced, written down or not. Saw: the skill deletes such a test with nothing in its place. The decision covers only written rules: 'A test that enforces a written rule on the code's shape ... is ported' and 'A test that checks ... a behavior no story or rule names, is an orphan, and is deleted'. So this is also a tension between the story and the decision, which /plan-sprint may need to settle. Evidence: core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT, the Read step 4 and the Sort table rows 'port' and 'delete, as an orphan'.
note: two readings: a legacy test that enforces a rule no decision, practice, or rules file writes down is sorted 'delete, as an orphan' with no call, question, or issue; the first reading: only a written rule must stay checked; the second: any rule the old suite enforced, written or not, must stay checked; the first rests on decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically, Choice: 'A test that enforces a written rule on the code's shape ... is ported' and a test of 'a behavior no story or rule names, is an orphan, and is deleted'; the second on story retire-a-legacy-suite: 'so that the old suite neither blocks my changes nor leaves a rule it enforced unchecked'

Where the harness offers the Workflow tool, the session starts the drain script once and the script returns only on done, waiting, stuck, paused (950 agents), or failed; a sprint whose stages chain with --after drains in one script call, because next issues each dependent stage as its predecessor closes. sprint-document.md step 6 says: 'Mark an entry in progress when the drain that runs its build task starts', so every stage, blocked ones included, goes in progress at drain start; drain.md 'When it returns' step 3 says: 'mark the entry for each task in closed whose outcome is done as done', so every stage goes done at once when the whole drain returns. The checklist shows nothing landing during the run. The story promises: 'the stages of a running sprint shown as a live checklist in my session, each marked as it lands, so that I can follow a long run without opening the completion report.' Saw: in the Workflow form, the default where the harness offers it, no entry is marked as its stage lands; the owner sees all stages in progress until the run ends, then all done. Note: decision task-tools-mirror-the-report accepts this ('Where a Workflow script runs the drain, the session marks each entry from the closed tasks the script returns, each time it returns'), and decision drain-runs-as-a-workflow-script makes the session wake once per drain, so the story and the two decisions disagree; the fix may be a script that returns per closed stage or an amended story, an owner question.
note: two readings: in the Workflow form of the drain, the session marks checklist entries only when the drain script returns, so a chained sprint's stages all show in progress until the run ends, then all done; the first reading: each entry is marked the moment its stage closes; the second: each entry is marked when the session learns its stage closed, which in the Workflow form is each time the script returns; the first rests on story watch-execution-progress: 'the stages of a running sprint shown as a live checklist in my session, each marked as it lands'; the second on decision task-tools-mirror-the-report, Choice: 'Where a Workflow script runs the drain, the session marks each entry from the closed tasks the script returns, each time it returns', with decision drain-runs-as-a-workflow-script: 'The session wakes once per drain'

The two readings: (1) each entry must be marked the moment its stage closes, by story watch-execution-progress: 'each marked as it lands, so that I can follow a long run without opening the completion report'; (2) marking from the closed tasks each time the script returns is what is owed, by decision task-tools-mirror-the-report: 'Where a Workflow script runs the drain, the session marks each entry from the closed tasks the script returns, each time it returns', and decision drain-runs-as-a-workflow-script: 'The session wakes once per drain'. Work item 'A test sprint writes support files first and runs its test tasks side by side' (and decision:test-support-written-before-tests: 'Each test task waits on the support tasks for the files it names, reads those files'): a test task is never told about the legacy support files its scenario uses. Path: tests tasks --stage write -> scripts/tests::stage_write -> support_of(plan, s) (s.support plus every plan legacy entry with sort=support whose scenarios name s) feeds only the --after waits; the test task's --files are its test path and old path, and its brief is scenario_brief(s), which prints 'Support: <s.support>' alone (scripts/tests:scenario_brief, 'if s.get("support"): parts.append("Support: %s." ...)'). {{TEST-WRITE-PROMPT}} tells the agent 'Your brief names ... its support files' and Read step 5 'Each support file your brief names, whole', and to record a helpers item where a helper is missing. So for a fixture a sort agent kept as legacy support (sorted_support derives entry.scenarios), the test task waits on its support task yet neither its brief nor its files name the fixture: it does not read it, and may record a missing helper for a helper that file holds, or write a test that ignores the fixture. At the base the test task held every legacy support file in --files, so it saw them; the change caused the loss when it moved support out of the test task's files. Scope: caused.

Nothing in the review prompt or step 11 limits a planner review to the items the assembly takes from that task. body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md in phase order (2 Frame, 3 Reconcile, 4 Dialogue, 5 Draft, 6 Resolve). The skill settles and drafts work at Frame, before Reconcile has walked the out-of-band changes. Reconcile's own rule says that must not happen. Frame, ruled sweep (SKILL.md section 2): 'For each ruled issue, carry the ruling's substance into the draft in final form — corpus delta, work item, or both — exactly as if the owner had just decided it live.' Frame, intake-drain kind: 'Run the issue walk (under Resolve) over that scope now, then the dialogue ... and the draft'. The walk's Promote step then says: 'Record the decision verbatim as the issue's ruling ... Then carry the substance into the sprint now, in final form'. Reconcile (section 3) says: 'The corpus catches up with such work here, before anything is drafted on top of it.' No step tells the session to re-base a final-form amendment from Frame, or a ruling recorded in the walk, onto a Reconcile outcome on the same artifact. An amendment carries the whole body ({{CORPUS-DELTA-FORM}}: 'Author an amendment by editing the artifact during planning and carrying the whole result'). So a ruled-issue amendment drafted before Reconcile can silently drop a 'Corpus catches up' change to the same artifact, or stand as a second amend delta on it. In an intake-drain session, the owner also rules each open question against a corpus that surface-corpus reads before out-of-band work is reconciled. The story promises: my goals, and the open questions and unreconciled work that bear on them, become one self-sufficient sprint that any executor can realize without re-deriving my intent. Saw: the phase order lets ruled and walked resolutions be drafted on top of unreconciled work. The skill gives no step that merges the two, so the executor or certification would have to re-derive which body is meant. Evidence: SKILL.md section 2 lines quoted above (Frame, 'Pull in the ruled issues first' and the 'Intake-drain sprint' bullet), section 3 first paragraph, and the section 6 'Promote' paragraph.

body: Reviewed the port path end to end: the sort prompt (core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT) says only 'A port's check is a program outside every test path, such as checks/<rule>, that takes the changed files' paths as arguments'. The legacy prompt (TEST-LEGACY-PROMPT step 2) says 'write the check at the path the brief names, outside every test path' and records 'command="<the command review checks runs, such as python3 checks/<rule>>"'. Then scripts/tests cmd_ports appends every recorded command to .ok-planner/review/config.json checks with no test-runner check (lines 1822-1837), and complete_failures only checks that each command is present (lines 2041-2043). Nothing in either prompt or either verb keeps the command from starting with a test runner, as a straight port of a pytest or jest fitness test naturally does. scripts/review cmd_checks then refuses the whole checks list. The story promises: the old suite does not leave a rule it enforced unchecked. Decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically says: 'A rule a fitness check enforced still needs a check after the test goes, and the review loop's checks run on every review.' body: Reviewed the sprint execution boilerplate's close (step 13 of 'How to execute this sprint') in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md, the one place sprint certification's calls are put to the owner for veto. Step 13 renders the completion report with the build's and the certification's calls, then runs review certified, and says: 'Where it prints `SPRINT NOT COMPLETE`, name each failure to the owner and stop: it is a genuine blocker under step 11. Then present the completion report's `## Calls` table to the owner, and ask which rows, if any, the owner vetoes.' So on SPRINT NOT COMPLETE the session stops before the veto question, and no text returns it to the question once the blocker clears; the calls sit only in the report file, where the owner can overturn one only by filing an issue by hand. Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_sprint/shared.md:{{CEREMONY-ARCHIVE}}, step 2. What the text does: it tells the session to commit the run's paths with 'git commit -- <paths>', 'naming only paths that exist or that `git mv` removed'. A documentation sprint's drop item runs 'git rm <file>' ({{DOC-WRITE-PROMPT}} in skills/plan-docs/core.md: 'Any other drop runs `git rm <file>`'), so the dropped path neither exists nor was removed by git mv, and a session that follows the text leaves the removal out of the commit. Harm (A3, story keep-documentation-current): the commit keeps the dropped document; 'docs stamp' then stamps the docspec at that commit and 'docs window' reports it current, and for a retired docspec the stamp removes its run state, so no later window finds the file: the committed documentation keeps a file the run dropped, and the work item's promised drop never lands. From failure i26 (driver t32).

A documentation sprint's drop ('git rm <file>', plan-docs core.md) and a test sprint's deletion ('git rm <file>', plan-tests core.md) are removed paths HEAD holds, so the session names them and the commit carries the removal; an untracked file's old mv path, which git commit -- would refuse, stays excluded. note: Limited each planner review to the items the assembly takes from its task. body: In a scratch project trued up from the working tree (stack run run-ef8c25237266), I wrote an approved sprint (one Amend story delta, one work item, the fixed completion contract copied from sprint-document.md), then asked .ok-planner/bin/review certified --sprint at each step. The verdict was right for: delta not landed, check failing, no completion report, report with no '# Sprint certification' block, defect open, stuck defect not listed, drive never ran, unapproved sprint, archived with closed: stamp, and SPRINT COMPLETE once every term held. Two outcomes were wrong. (1) Before the base file is written, certified gives no verdict and points at a flag it refuses: 'review: .ok-planner/sprints/cc2c-greeting.md records no base commit (no .ok-planner/sprints/cc2c-greeting-base.txt); pass --base' exit 1; then 'review certified --sprint ... --base 2340d85...' -> 'review: error: unrecognized arguments: --base 2340d85...' exit 2. (2) A second approved sprint, cc2c-farewell.md, whose work item (farewell.sh) was never built and on which no certification ever ran, printed 'SPRINT COMPLETE: .ok-planner/sprints/cc2c-farewell.md' exit 0. Its completion report named the first sprint's ledger (.ok-planner/review/runs/converge-2026-10-24T090000.jsonl): 'item 3 (certification): holds: the return block names .ok-planner/review/runs/converge-2026-10-24T090000.jsonl, the find loop ran, every defect is settled, 1 stuck defects are listed, and the drive ran over 1 stories'. certified checks that the named ledger holds a review task closed done and settled defects, but never checks that the ledger certified this sprint. The story promises: a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered, so that done means the same thing for every sprint; the contract's item 3 asks for the return block of sprint certification run on this sprint. saw: SPRINT COMPLETE for a sprint whose approved work was never delivered or certified, and no verdict at all (a message naming a refused flag) for an approved sprint whose base file is not yet written.
note: certified-accepts-another-sprints-ledger, certified-base-refusal-names-a-refused-flag

body: Reviewed /converge drive mode end to end (SKILL.md, prompts drive, merge, fix, verify, backout, owner-list, drain.md, scripts/review) and ran its verbs in a scratch project (stack run, true-up, two stories, tasks init, review prompt for every drive-mode prompt, review drives, merges --source drive, snapshot, fixes, verifies, drives --confirm --dry-run, drives --confirm, a confirm send-back, a second round to stuck, backouts): the mechanics deliver find, fix, verify, confirm, and backout. The divergence: in drive, analysis, and defects mode, review prompt fills [SPRINT PATH] and [BASE] with the word none (scripts/review assembled_lines, default sprint none), and merge.md is the one prompt that never says none means no sprint (fix.md says 'or no sprint where that reads none'; verify.md says 'where that reads none, no ruling does'). The assembled drive-mode merge prompt then reads, at merge.md:52: 'Where none names a sprint, this run certifies it from the base commit none, and the drive stays inside its scope: apply the sprint catalog's scope test to the function you named, reading it at the base. Where the code stood the same at the base and the sprint's change does not reach it, the defect is real but outside the sprint: tasks item set <failure id> --state backlog ... and merge nothing.' In plain English, 'where none names a sprint' holds exactly when no sprint is named, so a merge agent that reads it literally sends every real drive failure in a drive-mode run to backlog, unmerged: no fixer, verifier, or confirm driver sees it, and the break leaves the run unfixed as an intake issue. The same inverted condition stands at merge.md:31 ('where none names a sprint and its change deleted a file, add --base none'), merge.md:34 (the C3 bullet), merge.md:46 (the C4 entry), and merge.md:84 (the close counts). The story promises: 'to have each break that check finds fixed, so that a change that breaks a promise does not reach my users unnoticed'; decision converge-finds-then-fixes: 'The fix loop has fixers work through that list once.' Evidence: assembled file .ok-planner/review/runs/converge-test/merge.md in the scratch project, line 108: 'Where none names a sprint, this run certifies it from the base commit none, and the drive stays inside its scope'.
note: merge-prompt-reads-none-as-a-sprint

body: I reviewed /converge sprint (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md, prompts sprint-review.md, sprint-pass.md, merge.md, owner-list.md, drive.md, skills/_sprint/shared.md, skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md steps 12-13 and the completion contract) and the review script's certified verb it ends on. The return block's text does not say to name a stuck defect by its tracker id, but certified requires that id. SKILL.md The return: '- `fixed`: defects `verified`, `declined`, `duplicate`, and `stuck`, by entry of the accept list or sprint class' and '- `intake`: every issue the owner list wrote, turned, or closed, by id, with its category; each stuck defect with its last verifier's note and whether its backout closed `done`'. Neither line names the defect's item id; the only ids it asks for are issue ids. scripts/review certification_failures: 'elif defect["state"] == "stuck" and not re.search(r"\\b%s\\b" % re.escape(defect["id"]), "\\n".join(section)): failures.append("stuck defect %s is not listed in the return block in %s" ...)'. In a scratch project, a return block that listed the stuck defect without its item id gave: 'SPRINT NOT COMPLETE ... - stuck defect i2 is not listed in the return block in .ok-planner/sprints/cc2c-greeting-completion.md'; adding 'stuck: i2' gave SPRINT COMPLETE. sprint-document.md step 13 treats SPRINT NOT COMPLETE as a genuine blocker and stops. The story promises: done means the same thing for every sprint; decision sprint-goal-read-from-the-repository: 'A stuck defect the return lists ... is the owner's to take up, and holds no term of the contract open.' saw: a session that follows the return's text, listing each stuck defect by count per entry, by its note, or by the issue id the owner list filed, leaves the contract open on a sprint whose terms all hold, so whether done is reached depends on how the session happened to word the block.
note: converge-return-omits-stuck-defect-id

body: Reviewed /plan-docs (SKILL.md, core.md, doc-sprint-document.md) and drove plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs on a scratch project. The skill text treats only a docspec with NO stamp as needing every claim checked, but docs window also reports status new for a docspec whose stamp the repository no longer holds (after a rebase), with that stamp still set. Diverging lines: SKILL.md step 2 defines "new (no stamp: its documentation is written whole)"; core.md DOC-PLANNER-PROMPT step 3 "For a docspec with no stamp, every file the layout calls for ... the run checks every claim in it"; DOC-CHECK-PROMPT "or in any file of a docspec with no stamp"; DOC-STYLE-PROMPT runs "git diff <stamp> -- <file>" and says only "For a docspec with no stamp ... the whole file changed"; doc-sprint-document.md step 7 keys full checks to "the docspec has no stamp" while its Window line records "its stamp or none", so the executor sees a stamp. The story and decisions promise: docspec-stamp-opens-the-window "A docspec with no stamp, or with a stamp the repository no longer holds, is planned as new: its missing files are written whole, and every claim in its existing files is checked"; documentation-claim-ledger "checks every claim ... in every file of a docspec planned as new". Saw: with doc-state stamp set to 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567, docs window --json printed "stamp": "0123...", "status": "new", "stale_claims": 0, reason "stamp ... is not a commit this repository holds, as after a rebase; the docspec is planned as new", while docs claims greet-reference --stale listed all 4 ledger claims (count disagrees); git diff 0123... -- docs/greet-flags.md printed "fatal: bad object 0123..." exit 128. A check item in such a docspec then gets only the ledger ids rechecked, docs complete passes with one claim per check file, and claims in the text that are not in the ledger are never checked, so the update can ship documentation that does not describe the product as it stands.
note: doc-prompts-miss-dangling-stamp-as-new

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md in phase order (2 Frame, 3 Reconcile, 4 Dialogue, 5 Draft, 6 Resolve). The skill settles and drafts work at Frame, before Reconcile has walked the out-of-band changes. Reconcile's own rule says that must not happen. Frame, ruled sweep (SKILL.md section 2): 'For each ruled issue, carry the ruling's substance into the draft in final form — corpus delta, work item, or both — exactly as if the owner had just decided it live.' Frame, intake-drain kind: 'Run the issue walk (under Resolve) over that scope now, then the dialogue ... and the draft'. The walk's Promote step then says: 'Record the decision verbatim as the issue's ruling ... Then carry the substance into the sprint now, in final form'. Reconcile (section 3) says: 'The corpus catches up with such work here, before anything is drafted on top of it.' No step tells the session to re-base a final-form amendment from Frame, or a ruling recorded in the walk, onto a Reconcile outcome on the same artifact. An amendment carries the whole body ({{CORPUS-DELTA-FORM}}: 'Author an amendment by editing the artifact during planning and carrying the whole result'). So a ruled-issue amendment drafted before Reconcile can silently drop a 'Corpus catches up' change to the same artifact, or stand as a second amend delta on it. In an intake-drain session, the owner also rules each open question against a corpus that surface-corpus reads before out-of-band work is reconciled. The story promises: my goals, and the open questions and unreconciled work that bear on them, become one self-sufficient sprint that any executor can realize without re-deriving my intent. Saw: the phase order lets ruled and walked resolutions be drafted on top of unreconciled work. The skill gives no step that merges the two, so the executor or certification would have to re-derive which body is meant. Evidence: SKILL.md section 2 lines quoted above (Frame, 'Pull in the ruled issues first' and the 'Intake-drain sprint' bullet), section 3 first paragraph, and the section 6 'Promote' paragraph.
note: plan-sprint-drafts-rulings-before-reconcile

body: Reviewed the port path end to end: the sort prompt (core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT) says only 'A port's check is a program outside every test path, such as checks/<rule>, that takes the changed files' paths as arguments'. The legacy prompt (TEST-LEGACY-PROMPT step 2) says 'write the check at the path the brief names, outside every test path' and records 'command="<the command review checks runs, such as python3 checks/<rule>>"'. Then scripts/tests cmd_ports appends every recorded command to .ok-planner/review/config.json checks with no test-runner check (lines 1822-1837), and complete_failures only checks that each command is present (lines 2041-2043). Nothing in either prompt or either verb keeps the command from starting with a test runner, as a straight port of a pytest or jest fitness test naturally does. scripts/review cmd_checks then refuses the whole checks list. Drove it in a scratch project (stack run run-19b5f912af32, since taken down): with a checks entry 'python3 -m pytest -q checks/test_arch.py', '.ok-planner/bin/review checks --base HEAD --key gate2' printed: review: .ok-planner/review/config.json 'checks' runs tests through 'python -m pytest' in 'python3 -m pytest -q checks/test_arch.py'; tests run only inside a test sprint, or when a person asks for a run, so take it out of 'checks' and exited 1. So a port written this way passes 'tests complete' and then stops every project check from running at review, the ported rule included. The story promises: the old suite does not leave a rule it enforced unchecked. Decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically says: 'A rule a fitness check enforced still needs a check after the test goes, and the review loop's checks run on every review.' Saw: a ported check that review checks refuses leaves that rule unchecked, and every other check too. With a plain-program check (python3 checks/no-shell-out), the same drive worked: review checks filed it, and it exited 1 on an app/greet.py that called os.system.
note: ported-check-may-start-a-test-runner

body: Reviewed the sprint execution boilerplate's close (step 13 of 'How to execute this sprint') in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md, the one place sprint certification's calls are put to the owner for veto. Step 13 renders the completion report with the build's and the certification's calls, then runs review certified, and says: 'Where it prints `SPRINT NOT COMPLETE`, name each failure to the owner and stop: it is a genuine blocker under step 11. Then present the completion report's `## Calls` table to the owner, and ask which rows, if any, the owner vetoes.' So on SPRINT NOT COMPLETE the session stops before the veto question, and no text returns it to the question once the blocker clears; the calls sit only in the report file, where the owner can overturn one only by filing an issue by hand. The story promises: 'a way to see every call made while I was away, so that I can overturn one'; decision converge-close-takes-vetoes: 'Every /converge run closes the same way, whatever its mode ... asks which rows the owner vetoes ... In sprint certification, the sprint's execution steps make this close', and it rejects the alternative 'Present the calls table with no veto, and leave the owner to file an issue by hand'. Saw: the veto is reached only on SPRINT COMPLETE. The same order stands in the test sprint close (plan-tests/test-sprint-document.md step 7 to 8, TESTS NOT COMPLETE as a genuine blocker) and the documentation sprint close (plan-docs/doc-sprint-document.md step 8 to 9). Every other part works: the converge close in drive/analysis/defects mode asks the veto over tasks calls (SKILL.md 'The return'); driven in a scratch project, tasks calls and tasks render --certification list build rows and cert:-prefixed certification rows (declined, duplicate, not-owed, rejected, unlisted), and issues file plus issues rule --text - recorded a vetoed row as a ruled product-intent issue signed with the scratch name.
note: sprint-close-skips-veto-when-not-complete

body: Reviewed /converge drive mode (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md steps 2-5) against this repository's review facts. Step 4 says: 'file one exec task per name it listed, with what review drive-command --role resource-stop --name <name> prints ... they stop what a driver that ended early left running', and step 2 skips every stack stop where drive-stack prints none. This project's facts (.ok-planner/review/project.md) print 'none' and tell a driver under '## Resources a driver starts' to open a run of its own with 'python3 plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/stack up' and end it with 'stack down', but '## Drive commands' gives no resource-start or resource-stop role line, so step 4 has nothing to run, and no stop line (the canonical one runs 'stack cleanup') ever runs in a No-stack project. A driver that ends early therefore leaves its run in the root registry with no later cleanup. The skill text also says nothing about a role the section gives no line for. The story promises: each verification run's artifacts are removed once the run is over (decision run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run: 'Its cleanup, run periodically, such as after a batch of drives, takes down each entry ... at least an hour old and that nothing still uses'). Saw: a run from an earlier drive still registered two days later. Evidence: 'python3 plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/stack list' at the root prints 'run-38d7f9ed9ef5  2026-10-22T10:15:40Z  no ports  /var/folders/40/skk5nmw521l5rq6yrw0x72jw0000gn/T/ok-planner-stack/run-38d7f9ed9ef5  name: reference-names-the-public-surface-526f99f3' on 2026-10-24; '.ok-planner/bin/run-group members run-38d7f9ed9ef5' prints nothing (exit 0); its folder is empty; '.ok-planner/bin/review drive-command --role resource-stop --name x' prints 'review: .ok-planner/review/project.md gives no line for the role resource-stop under ## Drive commands' (exit 1); 'review drive-stack' prints 'none'. In a scratch consumer project with a declared stack, the same skill path works: the stop line '.ok-planner/bin/stack down --name drive; s=$?; .ok-planner/bin/stack cleanup; exit $s' took down a crashed run once it passed the hour.
note: review-facts-give-no-resource-stop-line

body: What the product does: /converge's owner list (skills/converge/prompts/owner-list.md, lines 32, 42, 61) checks only open issues before it files, and neither the merge nor triage reads the archive, so a judgment the owner closed without a corpus change (an environment failure retired, an upstream issue answered after filing upstream, a two-readings question retired) is filed again by the next run that meets it. The two readings: (1) dedupe against open issues alone is what is owed, by decision intake-writers-are-gated: 'Deduplication against the slugs already present is the standing discipline of every writer into the intake'; (2) a closed judgment is a question that no longer needs the owner, so writers dedupe against the archive too, by story find-and-fix-defects: 'so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment'. From drive failure i24 (driver t30).
note: owner-list-refiles-closed-judgments

body: Reviewed /converge (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md, every prompt under prompts/, _converge/coding-rules.md, scripts/review, scripts/issues, triage-issues/SKILL.md). Also ran the mechanical find-to-fix path in a scratch project trued up from the working tree: issues file (defect issue naming app/store.py:save) -> review backlog (1 report; a suite-file issue settled with left_alone {accept.md: suite}) -> defect item -> review snapshot -> review fixes --round 1 (t1) -> tasks close refused done while the defect stood fixing (exit 2) -> fixed -> review verifies (t2) -> verified -> issues close --as fixed -> tasks calls 'None.'. That path works. The divergence is in how the owner list avoids handing the owner a question the owner already judged. The owner list checks only OPEN issues before it files: owner-list.md:32 'First read `issues list --json` for an open issue on the same harm; where one stands, write nothing', :42 '... for an open issue on the same question ...', :61 '... for an open issue on the same defect ...' (and the defect route: 'First read `issues list --category defect --json` for an open issue at the same site'). Nothing in the owner list, the merge, or triage reads the archive (.ok-planner/history/issues.jsonl, `issues history`) for a closed issue on the same question. So a question the owner already settled without a corpus change comes back on the next run that meets it: (1) a story that is always blocked locally (needs real hardware or a hosted provider) produces an `environment` failure every drive, and the owner list files 'every other drive failure at `environment`' as a tooling judgment issue whenever none is open; once the owner retires it in /plan-sprint, the next drive files it again; triage routes it `question` again, because a retirement is not 'a live corpus artifact' that settles it; (2) an upstream issue the owner filed upstream, which /plan-sprint closes `answered`, is filed again by the next run whose agent meets the same suite-file harm or records the same proposal, and triage keeps it open 'while the project shows the harm', so /plan-sprint walks it with the owner again; (3) a merge's two-readings `question` on a story the owner retired without changing it is asked again on the next drive. The story promises: 'so that I meet only the questions that need my judgment'; decision intake-writers-are-gated: 'An agent that filed every observation as a question would be an ungated writer inside a repeating cycle, growing the queue run after run' and 'Deduplication against the slugs already present is the standing discipline of every writer into the intake'. Saw: the owner list's dedupe covers open issues alone, so a judged-and-closed question returns to the owner's agenda run after run.
note: owner-list-refiles-closed-judgments

body: What the product does: {{TEST-SORT-PROMPT}} in skills/plan-tests/core.md ports a legacy test only where it enforces a rule written in a decision, a practice, release-boundaries.md, or a rules file under .claude/rules/; a fitness test that enforces a layering or naming rule no such file states is sorted 'delete, as an orphan', with no question, call, or issue asking the owner to write the rule down. The two readings: (1) the story owes only written rules a check, by decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically: 'A test that enforces a written rule on the code's shape ... is ported' and a test of 'a behavior no story or rule names, is an orphan, and is deleted'; (2) the story owes every rule the old suite enforced a check, written or not, by story retire-a-legacy-suite: 'nor leaves a rule it enforced unchecked'. From drive failure i30 (driver t37).
note: legacy-sort-deletes-unwritten-rule-tests

body: Reviewed the sort table in core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT. Only one row ports a test: 'It enforces a written rule on the code's shape, such as a module boundary or a naming rule. | port'. Its read list limits the rules a sort agent looks for to 'the decisions under .ok-planner/design/decisions/, the practices under .ok-planner/practices/, .ok-planner/release-boundaries.md, and the rules files under .claude/rules/'. Every other test falls to 'It checks the code against itself, or a behavior no story or rule names. | delete, as an orphan'. A project that is just adopting the suite has a thin corpus, so a fitness test that enforces a layering or naming rule no decision, practice, or rules file states yet is sorted 'delete, orphan'. The sort raises no question for it (by design, decision legacy-suites-sorted-automatically), records no call, and files no issue asking the owner to write the rule down. tests plan --show then lists it only as 'delete, orphan' among the other orphans. The story promises: the old suite does not leave 'a rule it enforced unchecked'. That covers any rule the old suite enforced, written down or not. Saw: the skill deletes such a test with nothing in its place. The decision covers only written rules: 'A test that enforces a written rule on the code's shape ... is ported' and 'A test that checks ... a behavior no story or rule names, is an orphan, and is deleted'. So this is also a tension between the story and the decision, which /plan-sprint may need to settle. Evidence: core.md TEST-SORT-PROMPT, the Read step 4 and the Sort table rows 'port' and 'delete, as an orphan'.
note: legacy-sort-deletes-unwritten-rule-tests

body: What the product does: where the harness offers the Workflow tool, the drain (skills/_tasks/drain.md, The Workflow form) returns only on done, waiting, stuck, paused, or failed, and the session marks every entry in progress when the drain starts (sprint-document.md step 6) and done from the returned closed list when it returns (drain.md 'When it returns' step 3), so a sprint whose stages chain with --after shows no stage landing during the run. The two readings: (1) each entry must be marked the moment its stage closes, by story watch-execution-progress: 'each marked as it lands, so that I can follow a long run without opening the completion report'; (2) marking from the closed tasks each time the script returns is what is owed, by decision task-tools-mirror-the-report: 'Where a Workflow script runs the drain, the session marks each entry from the closed tasks the script returns, each time it returns', and decision drain-runs-as-a-workflow-script: 'The session wakes once per drain'. A fix under (1) needs a script that returns per closed stage or another channel to the checklist; under (2), the story's wording. From drive failure i32 (driver t48).
note: workflow-drain-marks-stages-only-on-return

body: Reviewed the sprint execution boilerplate (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md, How to execute step 6 and step 7) and the drain it reads (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_tasks/drain.md, The Workflow form). Where the harness offers the Workflow tool, the session starts the drain script once and the script returns only on done, waiting, stuck, paused (950 agents), or failed; a sprint whose stages chain with --after drains in one script call, because next issues each dependent stage as its predecessor closes. sprint-document.md step 6 says: 'Mark an entry in progress when the drain that runs its build task starts', so every stage, blocked ones included, goes in progress at drain start; drain.md 'When it returns' step 3 says: 'mark the entry for each task in closed whose outcome is done as done', so every stage goes done at once when the whole drain returns. The checklist shows nothing landing during the run. The story promises: 'the stages of a running sprint shown as a live checklist in my session, each marked as it lands, so that I can follow a long run without opening the completion report.' Saw: in the Workflow form, the default where the harness offers it, no entry is marked as its stage lands; the owner sees all stages in progress until the run ends, then all done. Note: decision task-tools-mirror-the-report accepts this ('Where a Workflow script runs the drain, the session marks each entry from the closed tasks the script returns, each time it returns'), and decision drain-runs-as-a-workflow-script makes the session wake once per drain, so the story and the two decisions disagree; the fix may be a script that returns per closed stage or an amended story, an owner question.
note: workflow-drain-marks-stages-only-on-return
